subject: Preflight: traffic provenance, token mix, and SLA mapping for TiltAI pilot
messages:
From: Evan Tran <evan@tiltai.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-10T15:07:00Z
Subject: TiltAI pilot — sample traffic and sizing context

Hi Chloe,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the latency and cost transparency you showed resonated with our infra team. We're lining up a small PoC and want to make sure the Dedicated sizing you propose reflects how our traffic actually behaves, not just steady-state RPS.

Quick context: our product mixes short transactional prompts (user messages, ~20–40 tokens) and periodic long-form synthesis (batched daily jobs, 600–2,000 tokens output). Most real-time calls are single-turn, but we have session affinity for context windows up to 3–5 turns (user + bot) for selected workflows. Peak traffic is heavily bursty: 80% of daily requests occur within a 3-hour window during business hours.

I'm attaching a small synthetic sample and a weekly latency report from our telemetry. For the sizing worksheet, could you confirm the exact fields you need (we have request timestamps, prompt tokens, response tokens, upstream wall time, and user region)? We can provide a CSV export to match your template.

Also, we care a lot about graceful degradation: if our dedicated pool is saturated, can you outline typical fallback behavior to Shared/Hosted variants and expected p95 increases? That will help our SREs sign off.

Thanks — Evan
Evan Tran
Head of Infrastructure, TiltAI
E: evan@tiltai.com

Attachment: tiltai_sample_traffic.csv (CSV, 42k rows sample)
Attachment: tiltai_latency_p95_week.pdf (PDF)
From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>
To: Evan Tran <evan@tiltai.com>
Date: 2026-11-11T09:22:00Z
Subject: Re: TiltAI pilot — sample traffic and sizing context

Hi Evan — appreciate the detail and the attachments. This is exactly the kind of provenance we need.

What we'll do next:
- I'll run the CSV through our pre-sales sizing pipeline and return a draft fleet footprint (GPU SKUs + reserve burst) and a short readout on expected p50/p95 token latency under the proposed configuration.
- Two requests from our side: can you confirm whether those long-form synthesis jobs are typically batched (single request producing the full ~2k token output) vs. chunked across multiple requests? Also confirm the KV cache hit rate (if you have traces) for sessions — even an estimate (high/med/low) helps us pick caching model variants.

Fallback behavior summary (short): Dedicated routes can be configured with automatic fallback to a compatible hosted model when capacity is exhausted. Typical observed effects for fallbacks in similar customers: p95 increases by ~2–6x depending on model variant and serialization overhead; we can set canary windows and circuit-breaker thresholds in the rollout policy. I'll include specific numbers aligned to the draft footprint.

I'll loop in Karthik and Marissa to help with the workload-to-GPU mapping and to ask a couple of quick structural questions about the CSV format.

Best,
Chloe Martin
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-12T14:03:00Z
Subject: Fwd: TiltAI pilot — sample traffic and sizing context

Karthik / Marissa — forwarding TiltAI's sample and note. Key asks from the customer:
- Model mix: combination of short transactional completion (chatty, low tokens) and large synth jobs (single-shot long outputs).
- Burst shape: 3-hour concentrated daily window (80% of traffic).
- Want fallback behavior numbers for SLA docs.

Please advise what exact CSV columns you prefer for our sizing harness and any quick heuristics you want me to ask Evan for (e.g., session length distribution, percent of requests using function-tool calls, typical sampling temperature).

I've attached the TiltAI CSV to this thread.

Thanks — Chloe

Attachment reference: tiltai_sample_traffic.csv
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-13T07:18:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: TiltAI pilot — sample traffic and sizing context

Chloe / Marissa — reviewed the CSV quickly. High-level assumptions and what I'd like Evan to confirm: 

Assumptions we can make now (from sample):
- Median prompt tokens: ~28; median response tokens (real-time): ~45.
- Long-run jobs: appear as single requests with response tokens around 1,200–1,800. If those jobs are single-shot they dominate GPU memory/latency for that request but are low QPS.
- Peak burst factor: instantaneous RPS during the 3-hour window shows a 9x multiplier over daily average.

Sizing heuristic I propose for a PoC (conservative):
- Primary pool: 2 x A10G-equivalent nodes (or 1 x H100 small instance) pinned for steady-state transactional traffic with autoscaling headroom for 2x burst in the short term.
- Large-job pool: a smaller, size-optimized slot pool for 1–2 concurrent long-form synthesis jobs (prefer larger VRAM or tensor cores).
- Latency target mapping: target p95 <= 350ms for transactional flows; large jobs expected at p95 = 6–12s depending on model variant and quantization.

Questions for Evan (please ask):
- Are the long-form jobs tolerant of chunked decoding (we can split and stitch to reduce peak memory) or must they be single inference runs?
- Do you have an approximate percent of requests that call external tools/functions or hit external APIs (network waits affect observed latency and influence routing placement)?
- Any strict SLO on p95 vs p99? You mentioned graceful degradation — does TiltAI have an explicit maximum tolerable p95 multiplier for fallback?

I'll draft a short footprint doc once we get answers; happy to bias conservative given this is a PoC.

—Karthik
Principal Infrastructure Solutions, Redwood Inference
From: Evan Tran <evan@tiltai.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samantha Li <samantha@tiltai.com>
Date: 2026-11-15T10:42:00Z
Subject: Re: TiltAI pilot — sample traffic and sizing context

Thanks all — quick answers below and attached the larger CSV export from our ops bucket.

- Long-form jobs: currently single-shot (the generation is done in one request). We're exploring chunking but not yet implemented; for PoC treat them as single-run.
- Tool calls: ~12% of real-time requests invoke an external API (lookup + enrichment) with a median external wait of ~120ms.
- SLO tolerances: for the PoC we can accept up to a 3x p95 blowup during fallback as long as the product degrades gracefully (timeouts and retries predictable). Production target is p95 <= 300ms for transactional flows.
- KV cache: approximate session cache hit rate is medium (~48%) because clients often include short-term context.

Attaching: tiltai_full_traffic_week.csv (CSV, 210k rows) and tiltai_latency_p95_week.pdf. We'll set up a short window next week for you to query sample logs if helpful.

Appreciate the sizing heuristic — Karthik. If you can send the footprint draft by EOD Tuesday, we can sync on Wed for the PoC runbook.

Best,
Evan

Attachment: tiltai_full_traffic_week.csv
Attachment: tiltai_latency_p95_week.pdf
